minutes.headline: Board says no town-wide reassessment is possible; abatements are the only remedy for the FY23 assessments.
minutes.summary: The chair opened by stating that no town-wide reassessment is available and that abatement is the only recourse. Public comment centered on the assessment crisis and the Board of Assessors' handling of abatements. The board then heard a pavement management plan and a trash and recycling update, made two appointments, and discussed a senior tax relief framework for a May warrant article. The preliminary budget presentation was deferred to March 14.

public_comment.topic: A board member asked whether assessments can be phased in gradually and what happens if Town Meeting votes down the budget.
A board member asked whether existing assessors could start non-lake abatements with later review by independent assessors.
Resident urged a public meeting with the Board of Assessors on abatement policy, land-only inspections for waterfront abatements, and asked who told assessors to hold waterfront requests.
Resident from Sunset Lane questioned objectivity of the investigation and argued the DOR process was not followed, calling it a clerical error.
Caller asked whether the snow and ice deficit would still be paid from the pavement management line and noted connection problems.
Resident asked how many full-time positions have been added since the current town manager started.

what_happened.line: The chair opened by stating that no town-wide reassessment is available and that abatement is the only recourse for the FY23 assessments.
Two appointments passed by roll call: a Council on Aging member and the ratification of an IT administrative assistant.
The board agreed that a member will draft senior tax relief warrant article language with the town manager and town counsel, aiming for a vote March 14.
The preliminary budget presentation was deferred to March 14, and members were asked to send questions to the town manager beforehand.
The board heard a pavement management plan and a trash, recycling and pay-as-you-throw update; the minutes record no vote on either.

why_it_matters: Residents who think their FY23 assessment is wrong are told the route is an abatement application, so how quickly the Board of Assessors handles those applications decides whether a bill changes.
A senior tax relief article is being drafted for the May warrant, so a Town Meeting vote on who gets relief, and how it is capped against the levy, is likely to follow.
The deferred budget presentation means the first look at the preliminary budget comes one meeting later than planned.
watch_next: March 14 Select Board meeting: the preliminary budget presentation, the priority list, and a possible vote on the senior tax relief article language.
The town manager's report at the next meeting on positions added since she became manager.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the Beale appointment, the main bid and pavement figures, the recycling fees and the Franco senior-tax-relief assignment. Most of the rest is only in ours (state aid, COLA, legislative priorities, deferrals). The one thing to know: our minutes record a ratification vote for Karen McCarthy as IT Administrative Assistant that the official minutes do not contain.
